correctness.rationale: For the stipulated on-chain X packet, multiplication by the weight-d logical X cancels the packet sites and leaves d−n sites. Multiplication by a logical Pauli preserves the syndrome. With g=−log p_gate>0, the assumed independent-edge sum is (d−n)g, while −log p_net≤g. For n≤d−2 the second inequality is strict; for n=d−1 equality occurs exactly at p_net=p_gate, including the central case d=3, n=2. At n=d the packet has zero syndrome and is not part of this comparison. Read RESULT.md lines 4–46 and VERIFICATION.md lines 18–32; this proof is analytic, so no simulation or certificate is needed. In the conclusion, ‘favored’ is weak preference, subject to the explicit tie.

value.rationale: The ceiling is a central design rule of the source. Showing that its local justification fails to change sign anywhere below d identifies exactly what the global decoder analysis must add. For instance at d=7, n=5 the packet still strictly beats the length-two complement even at equal probabilities. This is a motivated model-boundary correction, not a claim of full decoder performance or fault tolerance past half distance.
